response.sql: WITH team_avg AS (SELECT team_id, AVG(1.0 * w / NULLIF(g, 0)) AS avg_win_rate, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM manager_half GROUP BY team_id), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_win_rate) AS mean_team_avg FROM team_avg), diffs AS (SELECT t.team_id, t.avg_win_rate, t.record_count, CASE WHEN o.mean_team_avg IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE t.avg_win_rate - o.mean_team_avg END AS diff_from_mean FROM team_avg t CROSS JOIN overall o) SELECT team_id, avg_win_rate, record_count, diff_from_mean FROM diffs ORDER BY diff_from_mean IS NULL, diff_from_mean DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: A manager_half row's win rate is w / g. Rows where w or g is NULL, or g = 0, are treated as missing (NULLIF turns g = 0 into NULL), so AVG skips them. Records are pooled across all years for each team_id.
record_count counts every manager_half row for the team, including rows whose win rate is missing.
The mean of team averages is an unweighted mean over teams whose average is not NULL. diff_from_mean is NULL when that mean is NULL, and NULL differences sort last.

alternatives.interpretation: record_count counts only the manager_half records that have a usable win rate (w present and g nonzero), so it matches the number of records that were averaged.
